----README
JusPrin makes advanced 3D printing feel immediate: a confident path from model to machine that removes detours without hiding control. It is a dense, native desktop application for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a chat Agent beside the 3D workspace. Build every surface to feel focused, assured, inventive and approachable.

## Voice and name

- Write the name exactly as **JusPrin**: capital J and P, no space, never all caps in body copy. Set it in the surrounding text colour; never put the gradient on small text.
- Be direct, capable and optimistic. Never cute, cryptic or over-engineered.
- Prefer plain language to slicer jargon. Say "Slice plate", not "Generate G-code".
- Make the next action obvious. One `ButtonPrimary` per view names the thing the screen is for; everything else is quieter.
- Buttons and labels are sentence case, verb first, with no full stop: "Add printer", "Open printer settings", "Undo".
- Address the person as "you". The Agent speaks as "I". No emoji anywhere in the product.
- A status is never colour alone: pair the colour with an icon and a plain-language label, such as a `circle-alert` glyph beside "Printer offline".

## Logo

- Use the files in `assets/Logos` as they are. Do not stretch, rotate, redraw, recolour, outline, shadow or take the mark apart.
- Default to `jusprin-mark.svg` for application icons and small product contexts, and to the horizontal lockup when there is room for the name.
- Place the logo only on `neutral-white`, `neutral-mist`, `neutral-ink` or another quiet solid field, never over an image or pattern.
- Keep clear space of at least a quarter of the mark's width on every side.
- Minimum sizes on screen: 24px for the mark, 120px wide for the horizontal lockup. Below that, use the mark alone.
- Use the single-ink marks only when the gradient cannot be shown: `jusprin-mark-ink.svg` on light grounds, `jusprin-mark-white.svg` on dark ones.

## Colour

- Style product UI with the semantic tokens (`surface-*`, `text-*`, `border-*`, `action-*`, `status-*`). The primitives (`brand-*`, `neutral-*`) are the palette behind them, for brand artwork and covers, not a component API. The one exception is `Tooltip`, which is `neutral-ink` with `neutral-white` text in both modes.
- Page background is `surface-canvas`. Sidebars and grouped settings sit on `surface-subtle`. Dialogs, menus and popovers sit on `surface-raised` with an elevation shadow. A highlighted row inside them (hover or keyboard focus) is filled with `surface-raised-hover`, not `surface-subtle`, which would look sunk in on a dark menu.
- Body copy and values are `text-primary`; descriptions are `text-secondary`; metadata and placeholders are `text-tertiary`.
- `action-primary` is for the decisive action, the selected segment and text links. It is Orbit purple in light mode and Bloom pink in dark mode, so always put `action-on-primary` on it, never a literal white.
- Dark mode is a remapping of the same token names, not an inversion. Keep hierarchy, density and geometry identical and let the tokens change the values.
- The signature gradient runs from `brand-orbit` to `brand-bloom`. Reserve it for the logo, the splash screen, onboarding and rare hero moments. Never use it as ordinary product chrome.
- `axis-x`, `axis-y` and `axis-z` belong to the 3D viewport only. Never use them for status.
- A failed print or task is reported on `surface-failure-inverse`, a dark panel in both modes, with the `text-on-failure-*`, `status-danger-on-inverse` and `border-on-failure` tokens. Do not mix the ordinary text tokens onto it.

## Typography

- One family for all product UI: HarmonyOS Sans SC in Regular (400) and Bold (700), with the system UI font as fallback. There are no other weights and no italics.
- Use the ten type styles as they are and pick the nearest one; never set a bespoke size. `page-title` 24/30, `section` 18/24, `body` 14/20, `body-small` 13/18, `label` 12/16, `metadata` 10/14, each with a bold partner.
- Bold is for emphasis inside a run of the same size: the primary action beside secondary ones, the current row of a menu, a chip's name beside its detail.
- `code` (12/16, the system monospace font) is only for code, keys, file paths, commands and IDs. Names, words, numbers and measurements stay in the sans face; its digits are already equal width, so changing values do not shift.
- Letter spacing is 0 everywhere. Capitals are reserved for short eyebrow captions set in `metadata-bold`, such as "CURRENT SETUP", "STEP 1 OF 3" and menu section titles; type them in capitals rather than transforming the text.

## Layout and geometry

- Whole-screen structure (top bar, panes, where menus open) is in the Application layout section. Every screen in the design file is on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v), one page per page of the design file, and is specified layer by layer in the files under `screens/`.
- Design for a dense desktop application measured in device-independent pixels. Do not import web habits: no oversized controls, blur, glass or hero spacing inside the application shell.
- Space with the scale only: `space-4`, `space-8`, `space-12`, `space-16`, `space-20`, `space-24`, `space-32`, `space-40`, `space-48`.
- Controls take `radius-small` (4px). Containers such as cards, popovers and chat bubbles take `radius-medium` (8px), and so does `ButtonPrimary`, the one branded action. Sheets and large dialogs take `radius-large` (12px). Radii of 16px and above are for onboarding and marketing only.
- Borders are 1px `border-subtle`, drawn inside the box so a bordered control keeps its stated height.
- Control heights are compact: 26px for fields, selects and text links, 28px for chips and reply choices, 30px for a segmented control, 32px for a secondary or icon button, 34px for a primary or split button, 36px for a menu row.
- Shadows mark elevation, not decoration: `elevation-subtle` for tooltips, `elevation-medium` for menus and popovers, `elevation-strong` for sheets and dialogs. Flat surfaces carry no shadow.
- Every progress track is `component-progress-height` (4px) thick.

## Iconography

- Functional icons are Lucide 1.47.0 outlines, kept unchanged in `assets/Icons`. Inline the SVG and colour it with the surrounding text token through `currentColor`.
- Draw icons at 16, 20 or 24px. The only exception is the 14px fact glyph inside the setup card (`component-setupCard-iconSize`).
- Keep the JusPrin mark and product-specific symbols custom; do not approximate them with Lucide glyphs, and do not decorate with logo-derived shapes where a functional icon is clearer.
- No emoji and no filled icon sets.

## Components and states

- Every interactive component defines normal, hover, pressed, disabled and keyboard-focus states, plus success, warning and error where they apply.
- Hover and pressed change the fill, not the size: quiet controls go to `surface-subtle` then `surface-selected`; the primary action goes to `action-primary-hover` then `action-primary-pressed`.
- Fields show state on their stroke: 1px `border-subtle` at rest, `border-strong` on hover, 2px `border-focus` when focused, 1px `status-danger` with a message when wrong, and an `action-disabled` fill when disabled.
- Disabled controls keep their shape. Filled and icon buttons drop to 40% opacity, outlined buttons to 50%; fields, selects and chips switch to `action-disabled` and `action-disabled-text`. Do not hide a disabled action.
- Actions: `ButtonPrimary` once per view, `ButtonSecondary` for other labelled actions, `ButtonIcon` when a glyph alone is unmistakable, `ButtonLink` for low-emphasis moves such as "‹ Back" and "Undo", and `ButtonSplit` when the main action has alternatives.
- Entry: `FieldText`, `FieldSecret` for codes and keys, `FieldSearch` to filter a list, `FieldNumber` for one parameter, `FieldVerificationCode` for a six-digit code. Choice: `SegmentedControl` for two to five short options, `Select` for more, `Checkbox` for on or off, `Swatch` for a filament colour.
- Menus are a `MenuPopover` of `MenuRow`s, grouped with `MenuSectionTitle`. Focused tasks sit in a `Sheet`; an action that cannot be undone asks first with `DialogConfirmation`.
- Canvas tools use a `ToolPanel` of `FormRow`s. Status is shown with `StatusDot` and `Progress`, always beside words. `Stepper` marks position in a short setup sequence; `Tooltip` names icon-only controls; `DisclosureTechnicalDetails` folds away secondary detail.
- The Agent pane is built from `ChatHeader`, `PinnedSetupCard`, `ChatBubble`, `ChatReplyChoice`, `ChatAttachment`, `ChatTurnActivity`, `ChatToolActivity` and `Composer`. The header carries `ChipPrinterSpool`; the Home screen lists `ProjectCard`s and `PrinterCard`s.
- Draw every glyph with `Icon`.

## Accessibility

- Text meets 4.5:1 on the surface its token names; large text, control boundaries that carry meaning, icons and focus rings meet 3:1.
- Keyboard focus is a visible 2px `border-focus` ring, offset 2px. Never signal focus with a fill change alone.
- `status-warning` is the one exception in light mode, at about 2.5:1 on `surface-canvas`: use it for the warning glyph only, beside a `text-primary` label.
- `border-subtle` is decorative. A control must be recognisable by its label or glyph without it.

---
name: calibration-design-decisions
description: "2026-10-21 Kenneth's four calibration decisions, the verified reason a calibration cannot share a project, the runtime-only tower state, and where the UX page lives on the JusPrin v2 canvas (page id calibration, 8 boards, builder script)."
metadata:

---

Kenneth decided on 2026-10-21, before any code: a calibration is a project of its own
("acceptable, as long as we have a way to tell user what will happen"); the first tests
are temperature, flow and pressure advance; a result is saved as a named filament copy
(as the printer panel saves with persistAs); the physical-print ledger "doesn't matter,
whatever is the easiest". Entry points: the printer chip menu, the filament slot menu and
the Home card kebab each get a "Calibrate…" row; a symptom in the project chat leads to
the same conversation. No code exists yet; the tool guide's `calibration_generate` row
("onto a new plate") is wrong and must be corrected when the tool is specified.

**Why (verified by reading, not running):** every `Plater::calib_*` generator (Plater.cpp
~12677-13650) calls `new_project()` and then edits the single edited print, filament and
printer presets (`preset_bundle->prints/filaments/printers.get_edited_preset().config`),
so a test on a plate of an existing project would change every other plate. The test
mode itself lives on the current plate's `Print` (`set_calib_params`), is read by
GCode.cpp per layer, is NOT written to the 3MF and is reset to Calib_None on load
(Plater.cpp:5891). A reopened tower slices at one temperature; the PA pattern is the
exception (its per-layer commands go into the plate's saved custom G-code) and it
hard-codes plate 0's origin.

**How to apply:** the UX is drawn on the "JusPrin v2" canvas
(https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v), page id `calibration`
("Calibration · Printer & Filament"), boards `calibration-01…08-*.dc.html`, generated by
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_calibration_page.py`
(measures heights with headless Chrome; rerun it on a copy of `published/canvas/project`
with the live `canvas.json`, then publish with root + file_path=canvas.json + files).
Design points to keep: the agent says "I will save and close <project>; the test's
settings are temporary; nothing is written until you choose" before leaving; the menu
path shows a confirmation dialog with the same two facts; the result is a proposal card
("Save 225 °C to Gray PETG", saved as a copy, original unchanged) then a receipt with
Undo; a reopened test warns on the pinned card and offers "Regenerate tower"; the test
shows on Home as an ordinary project. Not drawn: Bambu's automatic PA path, flow/PA
boards, dark mode. Related: [[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]],
[[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]], [[printer-setup-connect-means-verify-and-save]].

content.text:
The "JusPrin v2" canvas now has a new page, **Calibration · Printer & Filament**, inserted after "Printer & Material Settings". It walks one temperature calibration end to end in eight boards, drawn with the canvas's own tokens and chat components and published as version 41: https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v

**What the page shows**, in three rows:

- **Starting a calibration.** Board 1 adds one "Calibrate…" row to each of the three menus that already exist: the printer chip, the filament slot, and the Home card kebab. Board 2 is the symptom path: the person types "stringy" into the project chat, the agent diagnoses, proposes a tower, and says in its own words that the current project will be saved and closed and that nothing is written to the filament until they choose. The reply choice is the confirmation. Board 3 is the dialog the menu path shows, since no agent sentence precedes it.
- **The test.** Board 4 is the test project, with the pinned card standing in for the setup card and an "Edit range" link as the manual control. Board 5 is the photo coming back, the agent's verdict with its reasons, and a proposal card that names the write exactly: a copy called "Gray PETG · MK4 calibrated", original unchanged. Board 6 is the receipt with Undo and the way back to the project. Board 7 is the test project reopened later, warning that the temperature steps are not kept in the file and offering to regenerate.
- **Afterwards.** Board 8 shows the test on Home as an ordinary project whose status line carries the result.

A note at the top of the page records your four decisions and what is deliberately not drawn: Bambu's automatic pressure-advance path, the flow and pressure-advance boards, and dark mode.

The builder script, renders, and the synced local mirror live in the figma-mirror folder outside the repo, and I saved the decisions and the verification facts to memory. Nothing in the JusPrin repo changed.

No, nothing on these boards is a temperature widget, and I have reworded board 5 and the page note to say so. What the boards reuse:

- The proposal card is the chat's ordinary settings change: the same "setting, old → new" rows a settings preview already produces, plus the name of the copy it is saved as. Saving is the existing apply on the filament scope with persistAs. No new card.

So adding a test is a declaration plus words, with no page code: the name; which OrcaSlicer generator; its scale, or for flow its passes; the setting it writes and in which preset; safe defaults per material; and a skill section on how to read the print. In code that is one entry in calibration_list's table and one paragraph in the calibration skill.

Two caveats from OrcaSlicer's side. Its generators do not share one parameter shape: temperature, pressure advance, retraction, max volumetric speed and VFA take start, end and step; flow is two passes where you read a number off the best tile; input shaping takes X and Y frequency ranges. So "scale" covers most tests, but the declaration needs a "passes" form too. And reading the result is the one part that stays per test, which is why it lives in the skill rather than the UI.

Short version: yes, almost all of it can be a skill plus one thin tool, upstream already treats one calibration's outcome as a new preset, and the outcome generalises to "one setting in one preset scope" for seven of Orca's nine tests.

## How upstream does it, and what to borrow

OrcaSlicer has two implementations and neither has a shared abstraction.

- **The dialogs** ([calib_dlg.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/calib_dlg.cpp)) each collect start, end and step, call one `Plater::calib_*` generator, and stop. The person slices, prints, reads the tower by eye, and types the value into a preset by hand. Nothing records the result. The knowledge is in the dialogs themselves: default ranges per filament type (the temperature dialog's PLA, ABS, PETG, TPU radio set), validation rules, and firmware notes for input shaping. That is exactly the content a skill holds, so the dialogs are a ready-made source for the skill text.
- **The Bambu wizard** builds the test off-screen, sends it, reads measured results from the machine, and has a Save page. Its flow-ratio save writes a new filament preset named "<filament> Flow Rate Calibrated" ([CalibrationWizardSavePage.cpp:37](src/slic3r/GUI/CalibrationWizardSavePage.cpp:37)). Its pressure-advance save stores the value on the printer under a name, not in a preset. So upstream already models one outcome as "a named filament copy", which is the decision you made yesterday.

Worth borrowing: the generators (they carry the per-test preset tweaks nobody should re-derive), the per-material default ranges, and the named-copy save. Not worth borrowing: the wizard's pages.

## What has to be code once the test project is open

Very little. The skill cannot do three things, and everything else it can:

1. **Generate.** Calling the generator is code. One tool, `calibration_generate`, taking the test name and its scale, mapping onto Orca's parameter struct, with the project-replacing confirmation in front of it. No per-test logic beyond the mapping, because Orca's generator already does the per-test preset edits.
2. **Survive a reload.** The per-layer steps live only in memory. Either a skill rule plus one workspace fact ("generated this session"), or a small fork-owned seam that stores the test's parameters with the project and re-applies them on load. The preset edits already come back with the project, so only the parameters are missing. I'd expect the seam to be a few lines; if so, board 7's warning disappears.
3. **Entry rows.** Three menu rows, hard-coded, as you said.

Everything else is already there or is text. The pinned card can be the existing setup card driven by `setup_record` (purpose "Temperature tower, Gray PETG on MK4", headline the range and what to look for), so no new component. Reading the photo is the model. Saving is the settings preview and apply with a named copy. The `calibration_list` tool from the guide is not needed: the tests are static knowledge for the skill, and the workspace already reports the printer, filament and nozzle. The skill carries the eight steps from the product definition: when a test is justified, which one, ranges by material, what to observe, how to read the print, which setting to write where. The on-demand skill mechanism exists in the app today but no skill uses it yet, so this would be the first.

## Can the outcome be abstracted

Mostly. Each test ends in one value for one setting, and Orca's own preset lists say which scope owns it:

| Test | Setting | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Temperature | nozzle temperature | filament |
| Flow | flow ratio | filament |
| Pressure advance | pressure advance | filament, except Bambu stores it on the machine |
| Retraction | retraction length | filament override, or printer |
| Max volumetric speed | max volumetric speed | filament |
| VFA | wall speeds | process |
| Cornering | junction deviation or jerk | process or printer |
| Input shaping | shaper frequency and damping | firmware, no preset at all |

So "outcome = a named copy of one preset with one setting changed" covers seven tests across three scopes, and the settings tools already save a filament or printer copy. Whether a process copy is supported today is unverified. Two exceptions stay machine-side: Bambu's measured pressure advance, and input shaping, which Klipper or Marlin keep in their own config. Those are a later, separate tool.

One rule to settle for the naming: a second calibration on the same filament should update the same copy, so "Gray PETG · MK4 calibrated" never becomes "calibrated calibrated".

> Generate. Calling the generator is code

generating what? gcode?

Not G-code. The generators build the test *project*, and the G-code comes later from the normal slice.

What `Plater::calib_temp` and its siblings actually do, in order:

1. Start a new project and load a stock test model from `resources/calib/` (a temperature tower, the retraction tower, the flow tiles as a 3MF, and so on).
2. Shape the model to the range: the temperature tower is cut horizontally so it has one block per step between your start and end temperature, then scaled for the nozzle size. The flow test instead gets per-object settings on each tile, one flow ratio per tile.
3. Edit the presets for the test (the global edits from the earlier table) and set per-object settings on the tower.
4. Store the range and step on the plate's `Print` object. That is the piece that matters most: when the plate is sliced later, the G-code writer reads it and injects one command per block, a new temperature every 10 mm of height, a new pressure-advance value every layer, a new speed per band. Without that stored schedule the tower slices as a plain model at one setting.

The pressure-advance pattern is the odd one: it has no stock model. It draws the lines procedurally as custom G-code per layer and parks that in the plate's custom G-code list, with a small cube as the object.

So "generate" means: model in, shaped to the range, settings set, per-height schedule registered. Steps 1 to 3 the skill could nearly do with existing tools (open a model file, scale, apply settings), but step 4 has no tool and is the whole point of the test, and step 2's cutting rule is fiddly. One tool that calls Orca's generator gets all four for free, and Orca keeps maintaining them.
